title: Engine response to operation: mutate (/io/response.json)
description: Stage 5, Tier 2 (protocol §5): mutants of the candidate's changed lines, one per change. Each mutant is the whole mutated file at /io/mutants/<id>/<file>, and nothing else in that folder. The core runs the tests of set T on the candidate with that file on top: a mutant that no test kills is a gap in the suite, not in the code. The descriptions travel to the Saboteur, which does not see the builder's code (§3): they state the operator, never identifiers or literals of the candidate. With a non-null error, the requested files stay unmutated and the core says so.

not_generated.description: What the engine could not turn into mutants: file that does not parse, is not of its language, or lines that fell outside max_mutants. A line with nothing to mutate (comment, docstring) does not go here. The core does not give PASS in the kill gate if anything is listed: what was not generated was not measured.

pruned.description: Equivalent mutants that the engine did not generate due to conservative AST pruning (protocol §5, Stage 5 step 2): a requested line where some mutant was discarded, with the reason. They do not count in the kill rate nor block PASS: they are not mutants, they were not measured. Empty if there were none.

id.description: Stable for the same candidate and the same lines; it is the name of the folder in /io/mutants.

line.description: Line of the candidate where the change is; one of budget.changed_lines[file].

description.description: What changed, by the operator's template (e.g. "arithmetic operator + changed to -"). No candidate code.

line.description: Line requested in budget.changed_lines[file] where the mutant was discarded.

operator.description: arithmetic: one binary or augmented operator replaced by another (+ and -, * and /, // and *, % and //, ** and *). comparison: < and <=, > and >=, == and !=, is and is not, in and not in. negate_condition: the condition of an if, while, conditional expression or assert, negated. constant: number ±1 (one mutant per sign), inverted boolean, non-empty string to empty (and empty to non-empty). return_none: return <value> replaced by return None. remove_call: a call used as a statement, removed (pass if the body is left empty).
